MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Work out 5,684 + 3,749. (1 mark)
   A. 9,443
   B. 8,323
   C. 9,333
   D. 9,433

2. Which statement about 63 is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It is odd because it ends in 3
   B. It is even because it ends in 3
   C. It is neither even nor odd
   D. It is even because it has an odd number of digits

3. A rectangle is made of 4 rows with 6 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 28 square units
   B. 20 square units
   C. 24 square units
   D. 10 square units

4. Which expression shows "5 more than x"? (1 mark)
   A. 5x
   B. x + 5
   C. x ÷ 5
   D. x − 5

5. The table shows the favourite fruits of 10 pupils: mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1. Which one has the greatest number? (1 mark)
   A. banana
   B. orange
   C. mango
   D. pawpaw

6. The table shows the vehicles that passed a school gate (10 vehicles): matatu 5, boda boda 2, bus 2, lorry 1. Which one has the greatest number? (1 mark)
   A. lorry
   B. bus
   C. matatu
   D. boda boda

7. What is 48 ÷ 4? (1 mark)
   A. 22
   B. 13
   C. 11
   D. 12

8. Write 2 3/10 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.23
   B. 23.0
   C. 2.03
   D. 2.3

9. Write 0.37 as a fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 3/7
   B. 37/10
   C. 37/1000
   D. 37/100

10. What is 4 L − 1 3/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 2 1/2 L
   B. 2 1/4 L
   C. 2 L
   D. 2 3/4 L

11. What is the next number in the pattern 9,000, 8,500, 8,000, 7,500, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 7,000
   B. 8,500
   C. 7,500
   D. 6,500

12. Which statement about 7,351 is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It is neither even nor odd
   B. It is odd because it ends in 1
   C. It is even because it has an odd number of digits
   D. It is even because it ends in 1

13. How many right angles make a full turn? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 2
   C. 3
   D. 1

14. A library had 4,250 books and 1,875 were borrowed. How many books remained? (1 mark)
   A. 2,365 books
   B. 2,475 books
   C. 3,625 books
   D. 2,375 books

15. How many lines of symmetry does an oval have? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 0
   C. 2
   D. 4

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. A library had 4,250 books and 1,875 were borrowed. How many books were left? Check your answer. (4 marks)

17. Wairimu had d shillings and spent 45 shillings. Write an expression for what she has left and find it when d = 100. (3 marks)

18. A book cover has 12 rows of 9 squares. A notebook cover has 10 rows of 10 squares. Which cover is larger and by how many squares? (4 marks)

19. Explain how to prepare a shopping list of three items and find its total cost. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — 9,433
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 5,684 + 3,749 = 9,433.

2. A — It is odd because it ends in 3
   Look at the ones digit. 3 is odd, so 63 is odd.

3. C — 24 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 4 × 6 = 24 square units.

4. B — x + 5
   The key words tell us the operation. "5 more than x" is written x + 5.

5. C — mango
   The biggest number is 4, which belongs to mango.

6. C — matatu
   The biggest number is 5, which belongs to matatu.

7. D — 12
   4 × 12 = 48, so 48 ÷ 4 = 12.

8. D — 2.3
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 2 3/10 = 2.3.

9. D — 37/100
   The last digit of 0.37 is in the hundredths place, so the denominator is 100. 0.37 = 37/100.

10. B — 2 1/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 4 L − 1 3/4 L = 2 1/4 L.

11. A — 7,000
   The rule is subtract 500. 7,500 − 500 = 7,000.

12. B — It is odd because it ends in 1
   Look at the ones digit. 1 is odd, so 7,351 is odd.

13. A — 4
   A full turn is four quarter turns, and each quarter turn is a right angle.

14. D — 2,375 books
   Subtract 4,250 − 1,875 = 2,375. Check by adding: 2,375 + 1,875 = 4,250.

15. C — 2
   An oval folds along its length and across its width.

SECTION B
----
16. (4 marks)
   Answer: 2,375 books. Check: 2,375 + 1,875 = 4,250.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the subtraction with regrouping, 1 mark for the answer with units, 1 mark for the check.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: d − 45. When d = 100, she has 100 − 45 = 55 shillings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for d − 45, 1 mark for the substitution, 1 mark for 55 shillings.

18. (4 marks)
   Answer: The book cover: 108 squares. The notebook: 100 squares. The book cover is larger by 8 squares.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for 108 and 100, 1 mark for the larger cover, 1 mark for 8.

19. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decide what is needed, write the three items with numbers, find the price of each, work out the cost of each item, and add the costs to get the total.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for choosing items, 1 mark for writing quantity, 1 mark for prices, 1 mark for adding the costs.
